newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Troops clash with protesters in central Quito.
newsitem.headline: Troops clash with protesters in central Quito.

text.p: Army troops clashed with thousands of demonstrators who ringed the presidential palace demanding President Abdala Bucaram on Friday heed the vote of Congress and leave office immediately because of mental incompetence.

Troops used tear gas and fired a few volleys of rifle fire into the air to disperse the demonstrators, who were angered by Bucaram's defiant pledge to ignore what he termed the "act of barbarity" he said Congress had committed in replacing him with Fabian Alarcon.

There were no immediate reports of injuries among the protesters, many of whom waved tri-color Ecuadorean flags and alternately chanted the national anthem and anti-Bucaram slogans like "son-of-a-bitch get out."
Thousands of demonstrators had initially taken to streets of the capital to celebrate Bucaram's ouster and the swearing in of congressional president Alarcon as interim head of state.
But the celebrations turned quickly into angry protests after Bucaram called his ouster illegal and said he had no intention of stepping down.
Two senior military officials arrived at the presidential palace early on Friday in an apparent bid to mediate an end to the crisis sparked by Bucaram's continuing battle for his political survival.
